title: helm(private): add configurable serviceAccount + PSP/PodSecurity hooks and values schema for init-jobs
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Private deployments often run in locked-down K8s clusters with stricter RBAC and PodSecurity requirements. The existing chart implicitly created a controller serviceAccount and assumed permissive pod security. This caused operator friction during installs in customer air-gapped clusters and blocked upgrades where PSP/PodSecurity or custom RBAC policies were enforced. This PR introduces configurable serviceAccount creation and names, updates the values.schema.json to validate new fields, and adds optional init-hook templates that emit PodSecurityPolicy/PodSecurity annotations when customers opt-in. It also stabilizes the init-job templating so upgrades/rollbacks are less likely to leave dangling jobs. Summary of changes: - values.schema.json: add "serviceAccount.create", "serviceAccount.name", "security.podSecurityPolicy.enabled", and validation for runAsUser/runAsGroup ranges. - values.yaml: document new options and defaults that preserve existing behavior (create: true, psp.enabled: false) - templates/serviceaccount.yaml: new template honoring name override and annotations for projected token and imagePullSecrets. - templates/init-hooks/validate-psp.yaml: optional init hook that emits PSP when psp.enabled is true; includes canary annotations and proper hook weights for ordered execution. - templates/init-jobs.yaml: refactor to use stable job names (release-anchored) and add ownerReferences so Helm handles cleanup on uninstall. - templates/_helpers.tpl: add helper to build serviceAccount name consistently across templates (prevent drift during rollouts). - charts/README.md: document upgrade notes and rollback guidance for clusters with podSecurity policies. Rollout notes and upgrade compatibility: Default behavior is no-op for existing installs (serviceAccount.create: true, psp.enabled: false). For clusters with PSP/PodSecurity enabled, operators should set psp.enabled=true and provide a cluster-level PSP or allow the chart to create PSPs (optionally restricted). The PR includes a migration note in charts/README.md describing a safe rollout path (enable in canary namespace, verify init-job success, then enable globally). Checklist: - helm lint, unit tests (values schema validation) - integration deploy to perf-canary k8s private cluster - manual upgrade test from last release (performed) - add docs and release notes - security review signoff (SEC-87) Tests and CI: initial CI failed helm-lint on templating edge-case (missing default for serviceAccount.name) which was fixed in commit 3; integration tests passed on re-run. No functional regressions observed in upgrade/rollback canary runs. Related: Linear ENG-2142 tracks broader private chart hardening and SEC-87 is the security review ticket for PSP/PodSecurity changes.

review_comments: Diego Marquez (reviewer): Can we make serviceAccount.create default to true to preserve behavior? Also request a unit test for values.schema.json to catch type regressions.
Asha Patel (author): Changed default to true and added a schema unit test in commit b3d7e4f.

Samira Gupta (security): PSP creation by charts is risky in some clusters. Please add explicit opt-in and document the recommended operator flow. Also request a note about RBAC bindings needed when psp.enabled=true.

Asha Patel (author): PSP is opt-in via security.podSecurityPolicy.enabled (default false). Added detailed instructions in README and added a note to the upgrade path. Marked SEC-87 for formal security signoff.
Ethan Cole (approver): Verified integration run in perf-canary and upgrade test. Approving pending SEC-87 signoff.
Samira Gupta (security): SEC-87 complete. Approving. Minor comment: add e2e to validate ownerReferences cleanup on uninstall (tracked in ENG-2142).
release_notes: Helm chart: add optional serviceAccount naming and PSP/PodSecurity opt-in hooks; improve init-job stability and upgrade compatibility. Defaults preserve previous behavior. See charts/private/README.md for upgrade guidance.
notes_for_ops: If your cluster has PodSecurity policies enabled, set charts.private.security.podSecurityPolicy.enabled=true and either provide a cluster PSP pre-approved for the chart's serviceAccount or enable the chart to create PSPs (requires cluster-admin during install). To roll back: helm rollback <release> <revision> will remove chart-created PSPs only if hook-delete-policy is set; follow README rollback guidelines to manually remove any cluster-scoped objects if necessary.
notes: Backported safe defaults to preserve existing installs. We intentionally did not change runAsUser defaults; customers should set security.runAsUser and runAsGroup in values for restricted environments.
